dorm-room.definition: A large bedroom shared by several students, usually in a school or college residence.

roommate.definition: An associate who shares a room with you.

resident-advisor.definition: A resident advisor is a person who assists students in their academic and personal lives.

common-room.definition: Describes a shared room in a school or dormitory where members gather for informal social activities.

laundry-room.definition: A laundry room is a space designed for washing clothes, often used for laundry or laundry.

meal-plan.definition: A written schedule sets out the meals to eat over a period, often a week, helping organize nutrition, grocery shopping, and time.

dorm-key.definition: A dorm key is a key used to enter a dormitory, often used for entering or leaving a dormitory.

move-in.definition: A move-in is the process of moving into a new residence, often used for moving into a new residence.

move-out.definition: A move-out is the process of moving out of a residence, often used for moving out of a residence.

off-campus-housing.definition: Off-campus housing is a type of housing that is not on the same campus as the student, often used for students who live off-campus.

club.definition: A spot that is open late at night and that provides entertainment (as singers or dancers) as well as dancing and food and drink.

organization.definition: The act of forming or establishing something.

fraternity.definition: A social club for male undergraduates.

sorority.definition: A social club for female undergraduates.

student-government.definition: A group of students elected or appointed to represent their peers to school leaders and staff.

newspaper.definition: Cheap paper made from wood pulp and used for printing newspapers.

radio-station.definition: Describes a radio station, the act of broadcasting, or material and procedures related to the station’s daily operations.

volunteer.definition: A person who freely helps without being paid.

intramural-sports.definition: Intramural sports is a type of sports that is held during the school year, often used for intramural sports.

drama-club.definition: A drama club is a group of students who participate in drama and related activities, often used for drama.

party.definition: An organization to gain political power.

concert.definition: To contrive (a plan) by mutual agreement.

game-day.definition: A day on which an important school or university sports game is held.
game-day.exampleUsage: Students wore school colors on game day.

tailgate.definition: To follow at a dangerously close distance.

study-date.definition: An informal meeting arranged so two or more people can study together.
study-date.exampleUsage: They planned a study date at the library.

coffee-shop.definition: A small eating place that serves beverages and simple food.

food-court.definition: An area, often in a shopping mall, where several fast-food outlets surround a shared dining space.

movie-night.definition: An evening set aside for watching a film, usually as a social activity.
movie-night.exampleUsage: The residence hall organized a movie night.

road-trip.definition: A journey made by car over a relatively long distance, usually with several stops.
road-trip.exampleUsage: The student club planned a road trip during the break.

spring-formal.definition: A formal social event, often a dance, held by a school or student group in spring.
spring-formal.exampleUsage: The student association announced the date of the spring formal.

tuition.definition: A fee paid for instruction (especially for higher education).

scholarship.definition: Financial aid provided to a student on the basis of academic merit.

financial-aid.definition: Money, grants, or other support helps students cover the cost of attending school.

student-loan.definition: Money borrowed to help pay education costs and repaid under agreed terms.
student-loan.exampleUsage: The financial-aid office explained the student-loan terms.

work-study.definition: A program that allows eligible students to earn money through part-time work while studying.
work-study.exampleUsage: She has a work-study job in the campus library.

part-time-job.definition: Paid work that requires fewer hours than a full-time job.
part-time-job.exampleUsage: He has a part-time job after classes.

budget.definition: A sum of money allocated for a particular purpose.

textbook-cost.definition: The amount of money required to buy or rent textbooks for a course.
textbook-cost.exampleUsage: The syllabus lists the expected textbook cost.

student-discount.definition: A reduced charge that businesses offer people enrolled in school for products or services.
